summary: Feed s116_double to IDS is degraded: 2 faults found - 82.3% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% IDS tolerance and microbursts to 1.56 Gbps overload the 1 Gbps IDS port (156% capacity, 4 intervals).

findings.root_cause: 82.3% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/HTTPS) vs IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is forwarded encrypted without broker-based decryption or keys, so IDS sees only headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection and is blind to ~82% of traffic; signatures and anomaly detection cannot fire on encrypted payloads, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot analyze encrypted payloads. Decrypt relevant TLS flows (with keys or via SSL visibility appliance/proxy) before the IDS and re-encrypt or filter as policy requires, to restore payload visibility within tolerance.

findings.root_cause: Peak 1.56 Gbps in 1ms bursts vs 1 Gbps IDS port (156% of capacity, 4 overloaded intervals). Packet broker is sending line-rate bursts to a single 1G tool port without load balancing or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port buffer overrun causes indiscriminate packet drops during bursts; even though average may look okay, burst drops create gaps in flows and missed detections, especially since IDS needs both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2+ IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port peaks <80% (0.8 Gbps) and preserve both directions per flow to same tool, preventing burst drops without slicing payload.
